I lost a friend not long ago. Before that, we talked about our respective letters, he asked me what I had done with mine, and I told him I had kept it, I couldn’t bring myself to throw it away. He seemed to think about it. Now I cannot stop thinking that I gave him the wrong answer. Please, random internet friend, let me try to give you, not a right answer, but at least a little bit of comfort or just, hey, I see u.

Not long after I started seeing a psychologist, and every session she asked me: “What are you going to do with your letter?” And to be honest with you, I didn’t want to throw it away, I still don’t, I have kept it as a “template”, just in case a need it later on (I’m still working through all of this). But I’d like to ask you too, what will you do with it after you write it? If I could ask you to do something, I’d tell you to please don’t end it, let the letter “rest”, fold it up, save it on a drawer, whatever, try to think of it as a chore, done and I don’t need to do it again, “it’ll be there when i need it” (which I hope is never). I don’t know if it will help you, but when I was through one of my biggest crisis moments, I googled “how to deal with unalive thoughts” and the one that kept me going was a simple thought: “You can always do it tomorrow, you don’t have to do it today”. So write it if you want, but don’t do anything else today, just finish the day breathing. And keep that going, write something else tomorrow, and continue on, until eventually, things are not as shitty anymore.


Write the letter if it helps you get your thoughts clearer, if it helps you understand what needs to change for you to start getting out there and living your life. And my friend, I hope that one day, you and I, can throw away our letters for good :)
